subject: StorWave POC — KPI charter, measurement plan, and owner commitments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@storwave.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@storwave.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: StorWave POC — post-call recap + proposed KPI charter and owners

Hi Elena / Samir — thanks again for the call today. Below is a tight recap and the KPI charter we think will make the POC actionable. Please confirm or flag items that need adjustment.

TL;DR (asks):
- Confirm the sample prompt set and user flows we should evaluate (I attached storwave_sample_prompt_set.csv).
- Agree to the measurement window and SLA targets below.
- Confirm the primary Redwood owners for each KPI so we can lock in the MA Plan.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks, warm-start):
- Workloads: 3 conversational flows + 2 batch reranking jobs (see attachment).
- Traffic shape: synthetic burst tests (120 req/s sustained for 5m, 300 req/s spikes) + shadow production traces for quality evaluation.
- Environment: Redwood hosted trial account (sandbox) with a /dedicated/ pool for consistent latency testing.

KPI charter (measure & gate):
1) Latency (user-facing generation):
   - Target: p50 < 200 ms, p95 < 450 ms at specified throughput.
   - Measurement: full-stack response time (API entry -> last token flush). Track cold vs warm (include KV cache warm-up period).
2) Throughput / TPS:
   - Target: sustain 120 req/s for 5 minutes with 95% success (200). Spike handling: graceful degradation beyond commit.
   - Measurement: simulated load runner & production traces.
3) Cost per token (unit economics):
   - Target: blended cost/token <= $0.00045 (model + infra + overhead) for bulk gen workloads.
   - Measurement: token accounting from Redwood usage logs with sample weighting.
4) Quality (intent accuracy & hallucination tolerance):
   - Target: intent classification accuracy >= 92% on the sample set; hallucination rate < 3% for fact-based prompts.
   - Measurement: hand-labeled ground truth on a 500-prompt sample (we propose to run annotation with StorWave QA).
5) Error rate / reliability:
   - Target: system error rate < 0.5% during test windows; graceful fallback enabled.

Owners (Redwood):
- Latency & throughput measurement: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com) — infra tuning, batching, and VM sizing.
- Cost accounting: Monica Patel (monica.patel@redwood.com) — token metrics and billing reconciliation.
- Quality evaluation & eval harness: Jordan Blake (jordan.blake@redwood.com) — sample set, annotation plan, and threshold checks.

Proposed timeline / milestones:
- Thu 31 Mar: Redwood delivers baseline smoke tests + evaluation doc (redwood_eval_template.xlsx attached).
- Fri 1 Apr: StorWave confirms sample set and agrees annotation owners.
- Mon 4 Apr – Fri 8 Apr: POC run window (metric collection + two scheduled load tests).
- Mon 11 Apr: Findings readout + decision (go/no-go to Dedicated).

Next steps: please confirm the targets above (esp. cost/token and quality thresholds) and whether StorWave can provide a small annotated sample or if you want Redwood to manage labeling.

Attachments: storwave_sample_prompt_set.csv, redwood_eval_template.xlsx, MA-Plan draft (ma-plan-storwave.pdf).

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: StorWave POC — KPI charter, measurement plan, and owner commitments

Jordan — quick follow-up after I ran this past Samir and our ML team. We agree with the latency and throughput approach; a couple of asks: 

- Add an explicit pre-warm period in the plan (we'd like a 20 minute warm window before the p50/p95 baseline runs).
- For the hallucination metric, please include a short definition doc so our annotators use the same criteria (example-driven).
- We can provide a ~200-label seed for intent + 150 for NER by Fri EOD. We expect Redwood to host the annotation UI or accept a CSV back.

Also, can you confirm whether the Dedicated pool you mentioned will have the same kernel-level optimizations enabled (quantization path) as Redwood hosted? We don't want surprises in production.

I'll attach the StorWave NER baseline spreadsheet after our ML sync.

—Elena

Jordan / team — noted. I'll own the infra test plan and make sure the Dedicated-like pool (sandbox flavor) runs with the same kernel family; if we recommend a quantization change I'll document latency/cost delta in the readout.

Quick operational notes: 
- I'll provision the sandbox pool by Friday 31 Mar and share access.
- Load tests: I'll run two scenarios (120 req/s sustained, 300 req/s spike) during the POC. Will include tokenization breakdown per request in the logs.
- Error handling: we'll enable the fallback policy to an N+1 smaller model for spikes; this will be visible in the infra trace.

Monica — can you handle the cost accounting and stitch the token counts to an estimated blended cost? If StorWave provides upfront labels, we'll include the annotation time in the billable estimate (transparent).

Ben Carter

Great — thanks all for the quick alignment. Finalizing action items below so we can add to the Mutual Action Plan (MA-Plan draft attached):

Action items & owners:
- StorWave: deliver seed labels (intent 200 / NER 150) by Fri 1 Apr EOD — Elena.
- Redwood (Ben): provision sandbox dedicated-like pool by 31 Mar, run two scheduled load tests during 4–8 Apr window.
- Redwood (Monica): produce cost scenarios and the filled redwood_eval_template.xlsx by 31 Mar.
- Redwood (Jordan): publish hallucination rubric + evaluation instructions and update the shared Drive doc.

Acceptance check (end of POC):
- All KPI measurements captured in redwood_eval_template.xlsx.
- Quality thresholds: intent >= 92% ; NER F1 >= 88% ; hallucination < 3%.
- Latency: p50 < 200 ms, p95 < 450 ms at agreed throughput.
- Cost: blended cost/token <= $0.00045 (or explicit variance scenarios documented).

If that looks right, we'll add these to the MA Plan and lock dates on the calendar. I'll schedule the kickoff for Mon 4 Apr and share the invite.
